title: Big Book Pointer
subject: ela
concept: A giant picture book on the projector; the teacher taps where to start, where words end and which way to read while the class shouts predictions.

title: Rhyme Time Rumble
subject: ela
concept: Two silly pictures pop up; the class claps if they rhyme and stomps if they don't. Syllable mode has kids clap the beats.

title: Letter Lanterns
subject: ela
concept: Each letter is a little lantern creature that lights up when its sound is heard; collect a full alphabet village.

title: Story Stage
subject: ela
concept: Drag characters and backdrops onto a stage to retell a classic folktale; the teacher asks who, where and what happened.

title: Meet the Book Makers
subject: ela
concept: An author and an illustrator take turns showing their part of a picture book; the class decides which job made each part of the page (words or pictures) and names the book's main topic and two details that tell about it.

title: My Story Strip
subject: ela
concept: Draw three pictures, tell the story aloud to the teacher, and label each panel with a word or sentence.

title: Sentence Train
subject: ela
concept: Word cars hook into a train; it only leaves the station when the sentence has a capital, spaces and an end mark.

title: Turn and Talk Wheel
subject: ela
concept: A spinner picks a picture prompt and a talk move ("ask a question," "tell more"); partners talk while a timer runs.

title: Blend Bakery
subject: ela
concept: Mix sound ingredients (sh + ip) into word cupcakes; real words come out of the oven, nonsense words come out burnt.

title: Echo Reader
subject: ela
concept: Read along with a highlighted passage, record yourself, and hear it next to a model reading. No scores, just practice.

title: Story Map Treasure
subject: ela
concept: Plot a story on a treasure map: start, problem, events, solution. The X marks the lesson.

title: Who Said That?
subject: ela
concept: Speech bubbles from a story float down; drag each to the character who said it or to the narrator.

title: Text Feature Makeover
subject: ela
concept: A plain page about ocean animals is hard to use; the class adds a heading, captions, labels and a glossary one at a time and sees which question each one helps answer faster.

title: First, Next, Last
subject: ela
concept: Order picture cards with transition words to write a how-to (making a sandwich) or a short story.

title: Word Zoo
subject: ela
concept: Sort word animals into habitats: nouns live in the meadow, verbs in the river, adjectives in the trees.

title: Context Clue Hunt
subject: ela
concept: A silly word replaces a real one in a sentence; use clues to guess what it means before the reveal.

title: Vowel Team Tag
subject: ela
concept: Vowel team pairs (ai, ee, oa) chase each other through a maze; tag the words they belong in before time runs out.

title: Moral of the Story
subject: ela
concept: A card game of public-domain fables: match each story to its moral, then invent a new fable for a moral.

title: Two Sides Theater
subject: ela
concept: Retell The Three Little Pigs from the wolf's view; voice the same scene as two characters.

title: Main Idea Umbrella
subject: ela
concept: Details are raindrops; build the umbrella (main idea) big enough to cover them all.

title: PIE Sort
subject: ela
concept: Sort texts by purpose: Persuade, Inform or Entertain. Pies get eaten when sorted right.

title: Hamburger Paragraph
subject: ela
concept: Stack a burger: top bun topic sentence, fillings for details, bottom bun conclusion. Missing parts make it fall apart.

title: Contraction Crusher
subject: ela
concept: Smash two words together into a contraction; the apostrophe flies in where the letters fell out.

title: Word Lab
subject: ela
concept: Combine prefixes, roots and compound parts in beakers; real words glow and get a picture definition.

title: Syllable Surgeon
subject: ela
concept: Operate on long words, splitting them into syllables and suffixes so the patient can be read aloud.

title: Character Choice Story
subject: ela
concept: Make choices for a character in a short story; the tool tracks traits ("brave," "selfish") and shows how actions reveal them.

title: Story Building Blocks
subject: ela
concept: Rebuild a scrambled short story, play or poem; each block (chapter, scene, stanza) must connect to the one before.

title: Headline Writer
subject: ela
concept: Read short news stories for kids and write the headline; compare yours to the main idea.

title: Structure Spotter
subject: ela
concept: Paragraphs about volcanoes, frogs and bridges; sort each by structure (sequence, cause-effect, compare).

title: Persuasion Poster
subject: ela
concept: Design a poster arguing for a class pet; reasons and linking words snap into place.

title: Dialogue Director
subject: ela
concept: Write a comic strip with speech bubbles, then convert it into prose with correct quotation marks.

title: Story Blanks
subject: ela
concept: Fill a story with nouns, verbs and adjectives; the silly result is read aloud, and wrong parts of speech break the grammar.

title: Idiom Illustrator
subject: ela
concept: Draw what an idiom literally says ("raining cats and dogs"), then flip the card to see what it really means.

title: Theme Tracker
subject: ela
concept: Read a public-domain story with a highlighter; tag details that support possible themes and see which theme holds up.

title: Genre Remix
subject: ela
concept: Turn a scene of prose into a script and a short poem; compare what each form does well.

title: Myth Museum
subject: ela
concept: Walk a museum of Greek myths; each exhibit links to an everyday word (Achilles' heel, Herculean, Pandora's box).

title: Blueprint Builder
subject: ela
concept: Choose a blueprint (problem-solution, compare-contrast) and build a paragraph that fits it.

title: Eyewitness vs Reporter
subject: ela
concept: Compare a firsthand diary entry and a secondhand article about the same storm; spot what each knows and misses.

title: Quote Picker
subject: ela
concept: For each reason in an opinion paragraph, choose the quote that backs it and write the sentence that introduces it; a quote that only repeats the reason fades out.

title: Research Rover
subject: ela
concept: Send a rover through a mini library of kid-safe articles; take notes on cards and sort them into an outline.

title: Grammar Garage
subject: ela
concept: Fix broken sentences in a repair shop: misplaced modals, wrong tense and runaway prepositional phrases.

title: Root Detective Cards
subject: ela
concept: Collectible cards for roots like "port," "graph," "tele"; combine cards to build and define new words.

title: Inference Interrogation
subject: ela
concept: A short mystery story; answer questions by quoting the exact line that proves your inference.

title: Character Face-Off
subject: ela
concept: Character trading cards from two stories; compare traits, motivations and themes in a head-to-head match-up.

title: Simile Slam
subject: ela
concept: Finish similes and metaphors fast ("as quiet as..."); the best fresh ones get saved to a class wall.

title: Fact Fusion
subject: ela
concept: Three short sources on the same topic; combine facts into one report and track which source said what.

title: Claim Court
subject: ela
concept: An author's claim is on trial; students sort reasons and evidence into strong, weak and irrelevant.

title: Essay Train
subject: ela
concept: Paragraphs are train cars; each coupling is a transition, and a weak one lets the cars drift apart until the order and the links make sense.

title: Slow-Mo Writer
subject: ela
concept: Take a fast sentence ("I fell off my bike") and slow it down with sensory details; a slow-motion animation matches your writing.

title: Comma Chameleon
subject: ela
concept: Place commas so a sentence means what the picture shows; one misplaced comma changes the picture.

title: Plot Rollercoaster
subject: ela
concept: Place story events on a rollercoaster (exposition, climb, climax, fall); see how the character changes at each drop.

title: Perspective Camera
subject: ela
concept: Switch a camera between first, second and third person on the same scene and see what the narrator can and can't know.

title: Summary Squeeze
subject: ela
concept: Squeeze a passage into 50, then 25, then 10 words without losing the central idea.

title: Argument X-Ray
subject: ela
concept: X-ray an op-ed: claims glow red, reasons blue, evidence green, and unsupported claims show up as cracks.

title: Debate Prep Desk
subject: ela
concept: Pick a kid-relevant issue (later school start?), build a claim with reasons and sources, then face practice counterarguments.

title: Source Sorter
subject: ela
concept: Sort sources by credibility and practice quoting vs paraphrasing; the tool builds the citation.

title: Discussion Dashboard
subject: ela
concept: Whole-class discussion tracker on the projector: talk moves, who has spoken, and question stems to deepen the talk.

title: Sentence Remixer
subject: ela
concept: Combine short choppy sentences into varied ones; pronoun agreement errors make the sentence glitch.

title: Word Thermometer
subject: ela
concept: Arrange near-synonyms from cool to hot (thrifty, frugal, stingy, cheap) and see how word choice changes tone.

title: Setting Swap
subject: ela
concept: Move a story to a different time or place and see which plot events and character choices break.

title: History or Fiction?
subject: ela
concept: Compare a historical fiction excerpt with primary sources from the same era; flag where the author invented and why.

title: Poetry Soundboard
subject: ela
concept: Remix a poem's lines with rhyme, repetition and meter; hear it read aloud and see the pattern highlighted.

title: Logic Gym
subject: ela
concept: Quick rounds of arguments: is the evidence relevant and sufficient? Streaks build reasoning muscles.

title: Two Authors, One Event
subject: ela
concept: Two articles on the same event side by side; highlight word choices and emphasis to see each author's spin.

title: Counterclaim Rally
subject: ela
concept: Volley claims and counterclaims with a bot opponent; each rebuttal must answer the last point.

title: Explainer Studio
subject: ela
concept: Write a short explainer article with headings, definitions and a comparison chart; preview it as a magazine page.

title: Sentence Diagram Builder
subject: ela
concept: Snap clauses and phrases into a sentence tree; build simple, compound, complex and compound-complex sentences.

title: Allusion Hunter
subject: ela
concept: Song lyrics (original, not copyrighted), ads and headlines full of allusions; tap to reveal the source story.

title: Dramatic Irony Theater
subject: ela
concept: Watch a short scene where the audience knows something a character doesn't; predict how the tension resolves.

title: Remix Lab
subject: ela
concept: Pick a myth or fairy tale and plan a modern retelling; map which elements you keep, change or flip.

title: Paragraph Surgeon
subject: ela
concept: Remove or move sentences in a paragraph and see how the argument weakens; restore the strongest order.

title: Fact Check Desk
subject: ela
concept: Two sources disagree about a fact; trace each claim to its evidence and decide which is better supported.

title: Claim vs Claim
subject: ela
concept: A group-chat argument about a school rule gets rewritten for the school board: sort each message into your claim, an opposing claim or neither, then write a formal paragraph that names the strongest opposing claim fairly and shows exactly where the two part ways.

title: Flashback Editor
subject: ela
concept: Rearrange a story's scenes into a flashback structure; preview how pacing and suspense change.

title: Pitch Deck Studio
subject: ela
concept: Build a short persuasive slide pitch; a checklist flags missing evidence and a media-motive lens reviews the ads you cite.

title: Voice Switcher
subject: ela
concept: Flip sentences between active and passive voice and see who gets the blame in news headlines.

title: Character Web
subject: ela
concept: Map a character's conflicting motivations from a public-domain novel; see how each pull drives the theme.

title: Tension Meter
subject: ela
concept: Track tension through a story with parallel plots and flashbacks; the meter graphs how structure builds suspense.

title: Shakespeare Remix
subject: ela
concept: Compare a Shakespeare scene with its source and with a modern adaptation; annotate what each version changes.

title: Rhetoric Spotter
subject: ela
concept: Sort speech lines by ethos, pathos, logos and devices like anaphora; then hear the speech with the devices highlighted.

title: Founding Words Explorer
subject: ela
concept: Read founding documents with plain-English layers, historical context and how phrases echo in later speeches.

title: Argument Builder Pro
subject: ela
concept: Construct a full argument outline with claim, counterclaim, rebuttal and evidence; a peer-review rubric checks each part.

title: Research Notebook
subject: ela
concept: A guided research notebook: question, sources, notes, synthesis and citations, saved locally in the browser.

title: Parallel Parking
subject: ela
concept: Park list items into parallel form; unparallel items scrape the car next to them.

title: World Lit Atlas
subject: ela
concept: A map of world literature in the public domain; open a story from each region with cultural context notes.

title: Tone Dial
subject: ela
concept: Rewrite the same paragraph by turning a tone dial (ominous, playful, bitter) and see how word choices change.

title: Page to Screen
subject: ela
concept: Compare a public-domain story with a shot-by-shot storyboard of a film version; discuss what each medium emphasizes.

title: Fallacy Field Guide
subject: ela
concept: Collect fallacy cards (strawman, slippery slope, ad hominem) by spotting them in ads and comment sections.

title: Thesis Workshop
subject: ela
concept: Turn a vague claim into an arguable thesis about a text; gather evidence that proves it and analysis that explains it.

title: Socratic Seminar Board
subject: ela
concept: Projector board for a seminar: question bank, talk map of who responds to whom, and evidence citations.

title: Punctuation Power-Ups
subject: ela
concept: Race through sentences that need semicolons, colons and dashes; each correct mark speeds you up.

title: American Lit Timeline
subject: ela
concept: Movements from Puritan writing to Modernism on a timeline; connect public-domain works to their historical moment.

title: Satire Decoder
subject: ela
concept: Read public-domain satire like "A Modest Proposal"; separate what is said from what is meant.

title: Premise Inspector
subject: ela
concept: Analyze the premises and reasoning in founding documents and later responses to them.

title: Source Mixer
subject: ela
concept: Combine text, chart, video transcript and image sources into one answer; track how each strengthens the claim.

title: Rhetorical Situation Simulator
subject: ela
concept: Change speaker, audience and purpose for a speech and see which rhetorical choices work.

title: Personal Essay Studio
subject: ela
concept: Brainstorm, draft and revise a personal essay with prompts that pull out specific details; nothing leaves the browser.

title: Usage Panel
subject: ela
concept: Debate contested usage ("literally," singular "they") as a dictionary panel; see how style guides have changed.

title: Globe Theatre Stage
subject: ela
concept: Explore Shakespeare scenes on a 3D Globe stage; switch interpretations and hear how delivery changes meaning.

title: Ambiguity Lab
subject: ela
concept: Change one structural choice in a public-domain story (ending, order, narrator) and see how the meaning shifts.

title: Argument Map
subject: ela
concept: Map a complex essay's structure into nodes and links; find the load-bearing claims.

title: Question Sharpener
subject: ela
concept: Start from a broad interest and narrow it into a researchable question; the tool tests each draft (too broad, too narrow, already answered) and maps what you would need to find out.

title: Speech Coach
subject: ela
concept: Rehearse a speech with a pacing meter, filler-word counter and slide timer, all on your own device.

title: Ad Agency
subject: ela
concept: Run a fake ad agency: craft persuasive campaigns, then switch sides and audit the tricks as a watchdog.

title: Word Family Tree
subject: ela
concept: Trace words back through Latin, Greek, Old English and Norse roots on an interactive family tree.

title: Classroom Phrases Game
subject: eld
concept: Picture prompts for classroom phrases ("Can I go to the bathroom?"); the class practices together with audio.

title: Bedtime Retell
subject: eld
concept: A sleepy puppet friend asks to hear a short story again; learners retell the beginning, middle and end with sentence frames and picture prompts, answering 'what happened first? then what?', and the friend drifts off after a complete retell.

title: Shape Talk
subject: eld
concept: Describe a hidden shape to a partner using sentence frames ("It has 4 sides"); partner guesses.

title: I Spy Science
subject: eld
concept: Zoomable nature photos with vocabulary labels and audio; learners describe what they see with frames.

title: Community Map Words
subject: eld
concept: A friendly town map; tap places and helpers to hear and practice the words.

title: Talk Moves Trainer
subject: eld
concept: Practice agreeing, disagreeing and adding on with animated classmates; choose the polite academic phrase.

title: Opinion Builder
subject: eld
concept: Sentence frames and word banks to build an opinion with because and so; audio read-back.

title: Math Explainer
subject: eld
concept: Record or type an explanation of a word problem solution using sequence words and frames.

title: Cause and Effect Rewind
subject: eld
concept: A picture story (a dropped ice cream, a missed bus) runs backward one step at a time; learners link each step with because, so or as a result to rewind it to the start.

title: Time Machine Talk
subject: eld
concept: Travel to the past and describe what you see in past tense; the machine only works with the right verb forms.

title: Summary Scaffold
subject: eld
concept: Graphic organizer that turns a text into a summary with citation frames and vocabulary support.

title: Word Problem Decoder
subject: eld
concept: Highlight math language (per, each, how many more) and see how it maps to operations.

title: CER Builder
subject: eld
concept: Build a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph with language frames for a simple experiment.

title: Perspective Frames
subject: eld
concept: Sort statements by speaker and use comparison language frames to explain differences.

title: Idiom Island
subject: eld
concept: Explore an island where each place is an idiom; learn literal vs real meanings with pictures and audio.

title: Counterpoint Frames
subject: eld
concept: Practice academic argument and counterargument language in a mock debate with scaffolds that fade over time.

title: Definition Duel
subject: eld
concept: Match math terms to precise definitions and conditions; spot what's missing in imprecise ones.

title: Chart Narrator
subject: eld
concept: Describe trends in real charts with language frames (increased sharply, remained stable).

title: Is the Historian Right?
subject: eld
concept: Analyze a historian's argument with sentence frames for causation and evaluation.

title: Inbox Simulator
subject: eld
concept: Respond to realistic school and job emails; a register meter shows formal vs casual tone.

title: Library Adventure
subject: library
concept: Walk a cartoon library; find picture books, fiction and nonfiction sections and learn how spine labels work.

title: Wonder Wall
subject: library
concept: Class wonder wall on the projector: sort questions into "look it up," "ask an expert" and "try it."

title: Keyword Fishing
subject: library
concept: Cast a search with the keywords you choose and see what you catch; too broad pulls in junk and too narrow catches nothing.

title: Credit Card Builder
subject: library
concept: Build simple source credits for books, websites and images; learn why creators deserve credit.

title: Fake or Fact Lab
subject: library
concept: Investigate made-up sites and posts with lateral reading; check authors, dates and sources.

title: Research Quest
subject: library
concept: A quest-style guide through the research process; each stage unlocks the next with a real task.

title: Boolean Builder
subject: library
concept: Build searches with AND, OR, NOT and quotes; a Venn diagram shows how each choice changes results.

title: Fair Use Review
subject: library
concept: Rule on fair use cases (memes, remixes, school projects) using the four factors; learn Creative Commons licenses.

title: Windblown Pages
subject: ela
concept: A gust blows the pictures off story and fact book pages; the class matches each picture, caption and diagram back to its words, says whether the author or the illustrator told each part, and names what the picture shows that the words do not.

title: Alike and Different Books
subject: ela
concept: Two books land side by side: a bear storybook and a bear fact book, or two Cinderellas from different lands. The class drops picture cards into two overlapping hoops to show what is the same, what is different, and which book tells a story.

title: Question Cube
subject: ela
concept: After a short read-aloud, a giant question cube rolls who, what, where, when, why or how; teams answer and tap the sentence or picture that proves it. Later rolls ask how a character met a big problem or how two facts connect.

title: Because Bridge
subject: ela
concept: An author's point stands on one riverbank; the class drags reasons from the text into place as bridge planks and reads the point aloud with because. A true fact that does not support the point makes the bridge wobble until it is swapped out.

title: Poem Drum
subject: ela
concept: First the class decides whether a page is a poem or a story; then the poem scrolls while a drum taps its beat, kids clap along and tap the rhymes, repeated lines and feeling words, and they record a reading in time with the drum.

title: Vocabulary Jar
subject: ela
concept: During a read-aloud, kids tap any word they wonder about; the class uses the picture and nearby words to work it out, drops it in the class jar, and the jar sparkles each time someone uses that word to describe something later.

title: Big Question Chart
subject: ela
concept: The class picks a question (How do frogs grow?), reads picture books and recalls what they have seen, and pins each fact to a big chart under the part of the answer it helps; the chart becomes a shared report the class reads back together.

title: Owl Wants More
subject: ela
concept: A short class story looks thin; a curious owl keeps asking (What color? Where? How did it feel?), and each detail the class adds grows into the picture. A last polish fixes capitals and end marks before the puppet reads the better story aloud.

title: Show and Tell Spotlight
subject: ela
concept: A child picks an object card, adds a quick drawing, and tells about it in full sentences while detail stars light up for color, size and use; a switch changes the listener from a best friend to the principal so kids hear how talk changes.

title: Class Phone Call
subject: ela
concept: A friendly caller phones the class with a short story or news (a lost kite, a new baby goat); the class takes turns asking the caller questions to learn more, then answers the caller's quiz about the key details.

title: I Choose Because
subject: eld
concept: Two pictures offer a choice (a pet fish or a hamster, a reading corner or a block corner); learners pick one and say why with frames (I choose ___ because ___), then answer a friend's choice with I agree or I disagree because.

title: Draft Car Wash
subject: ela
concept: A rough draft rolls through a car wash with stations for add, cut, move and polish; students pick changes for a named reader and purpose, fix capitals, commas and spelling at the last station, and compare the clean draft with the original.

title: Radio Hour Notes
subject: ela
concept: A short kids' radio show plays a field trip report and a guest arguing for a longer recess; students pause to note the main points, then sort the guest's claims into backed by reasons, backed by evidence, or not backed at all.

title: Planetarium Guide
subject: ela
concept: Students plan a short planetarium talk: order the stops, attach a picture or sound to each, rehearse with a pace meter, then switch the audience from kindergartners to visiting scientists and hear how their word choice and formality should change.

title: Script Read-Through
subject: ela
concept: Small groups take parts in a short script and rehearse with a scrolling prompter that marks pace and pauses; tapping a tricky long word splits it into syllables and word parts, and each group performs and replays its recording.

title: Main Idea Pinboard
subject: ela
concept: Students read a short article or fable, write the main idea or central message on a card, then pin the exact sentences that prove it; a meter shows how many key details the card covers and flags pins that only repeat the idea.

title: Glossary Makers
subject: ela
concept: Students build the glossary for a short science or history passage: for each bold word they gather clues from the sentence, word parts and a picture, write a kid definition with a synonym and an opposite, then link two facts with however or similarly.

title: Mood in the Pictures
subject: ela
concept: A story scene appears as plain text, as illustrated comic panels and as a read-aloud with music; students mark what each picture or sound adds (a mood, a hidden clue, a feeling) and where a version follows or changes the words.

title: How It Works Diagrams
subject: ela
concept: A short text explains how something happens (a canal lock, a bill becoming law, a volcano erupting); students drag each sentence onto the matching part of a diagram, map or timeline, and the animation runs only when every step and cause is in place.

title: Swap the Teller
subject: ela
concept: One mix-up at a county fair is told by a first-person kid, a third-person narrator and a grumpy goose; students switch tellers, see which details each one includes or leaves out, then decide whether their own view matches the teller's.

title: Side by Side Reader
subject: ela
concept: Two texts open side by side (two books in a series, two articles on one topic, a story told in chapters and one told in letters); students drag shared details to the middle and differences to each side, then name what each structure does.

title: Show, Don't Tell
subject: ela
concept: Each card holds a telling sentence (Maya was nervous); students read a scene to collect what a character thinks, says and does, rewrite the card to show the feeling instead, and the class guesses the hidden feeling from their version.

title: Note Card Shuffle
subject: ela
concept: Students pick a question about an animal or an invention, read three short kid pages, jot facts on note cards in their own words, and sort the cards into the project's categories; an empty or crowded category shows what to look up next.

title: Draft Versus Draft
subject: ela
concept: Two revisions of the same draft go head to head; the class votes for the one that better fits the stated reader and purpose, and the tool marks each change as a cut, add, move or reword so students can name what made it stronger.

title: Theme Evidence Ladder
subject: ela
concept: Students propose a theme for a short public-domain story, then rank quoted passages from strongest to weakest support; the tool shows which passages also back a rival theme, and a poem on the same subject tests whether the theme holds across genres.

title: Claim, Quote, Comment
subject: ela
concept: Students build an analysis paragraph about an article: a claim, a quotation or paraphrase that supports it, and their own explanation; the tool flags a quote dropped in with no explanation or one that does not actually prove the claim.

title: Page, Audio, Screen
subject: ela
concept: A book club must recommend one version of a scene or news story (text, audiobook or film storyboard); members mark what each version adds, cuts or changes, then pick the medium that best serves a purpose, from explaining a process to building suspense.

title: Podcast Listening Club
subject: ela
concept: Students listen to a short student podcast where two hosts argue about a cashless cafeteria; they tag each claim as supported, unsupported or off topic, then discussion cards ask them to build on, question or challenge a classmate's tags.

title: Docent Tour Talk
subject: ela
concept: Students prepare a two-minute museum tour of one exhibit: order their points, choose one image or sound per stop, rehearse against pace and eye-contact checks, then redo the opening for a curator, a family and a group of second graders.

title: Context, Roots, Dictionary
subject: ela
concept: Students meet academic words (hypothesis, perspective, significant) inside short science, history and math passages; they try context first, then a Greek or Latin root, then the dictionary entry, and the tool tracks which strategy cracked each word.

title: Double Meanings
subject: ela
concept: Students sort lines from stories, speeches and ads into pun, verbal irony, analogy or allusion, explain both meanings, then swap one key word for a plain one and watch the tone and meaning fall flat.

title: Pause and Break
subject: ela
concept: A reading voice pauses exactly where the punctuation tells it to; students add or move commas, parentheses, dashes and ellipses until the sentence sounds the way the writer meant, including quotations with words left out.

title: Explainer Sections
subject: ela
concept: Students take apart a short explainer, such as how a vaccine trial works, to see what each section does for the reader, then build their own by choosing an organizing pattern and writing headings and transitions that fit it.

title: Blizzard Scenes
subject: ela
concept: Students write a short scene about a class trip stranded by a blizzard, then retell it from another character's point of view and in a different order; the versions sit side by side with questions about what each choice reveals or hides.

title: Memoir and Biography
subject: ela
concept: Students read a memoir excerpt and a biography of the same inventor; they tag where each introduces her, which anecdotes it uses and what each author wants readers to think, then compare how the two connect the same events.

title: Then What Happened?
subject: eld
concept: Learners narrate a comic strip or a personal moment one panel at a time, choosing time words and past-tense verbs from frames that fade as they go; a listener nods along and asks then what? whenever a step is missing.

title: Editors in the Margin
subject: ela
concept: Students revise a short essay by answering margin comments from three editors: one for purpose and audience, one for sentence variety, one for hyphens and spelling; accepted changes are tracked, and a before-and-after read shows which edits mattered.

title: Theme Ledger
subject: ela
concept: Students follow two themes through a public-domain story, logging each passage that develops them in a two-column ledger; a chart shows where the themes rise and cross, and they draft an analysis paragraph from their strongest entries.

title: Idea Threads
subject: ela
concept: Students pull a colored thread through a speech or essay, attaching it to each sentence that develops a central idea; a second thread for another idea shows where the two twist together, and every knot must be backed by a quoted line.

title: Portrait in Four Media
subject: ela
concept: A scientist's life is told four ways: an encyclopedia entry, an interview transcript, a documentary storyboard and a photo archive; students mark what each account emphasizes, check facts across them, and assemble one accurate profile.

title: Audience Shift Briefing
subject: ela
concept: Students turn a research finding into a three-minute briefing, then rebuild it for a city board, a neighborhood meeting and a middle school class, choosing evidence, visuals and register for each while audience reaction cards respond.

title: Key Term Tracker
subject: ela
concept: Students follow one loaded word (faction, liberty, nature) through a founding essay or a novel, collecting each place the author defines, narrows or bends it; context and a usage dictionary help with unfamiliar words, and the term's meaning card grows.

title: Pacing Strip
subject: ela
concept: Students write a short scene, then tag each sentence as action, dialogue, description or reflection; a pacing strip shows where the scene rushes or drags, and they revise until the turning point gets the space it needs.

title: Many Voices Book
subject: library
concept: Each child adds a page to one class book: a greeting from home, a favorite food, a game they play. The class reads it together, finds what is the same and different, and decides how to order the pages so everyone is in.

title: Windows and Mirrors Shelf
subject: library
concept: Students sort book blurbs into mirrors (lives like mine) and windows (lives different from mine), notice which kind their own reading lacks, then build a stack across genres and formats with both and say what they hope to find.

title: Rabbit Hole Notebook
subject: library
concept: Start from a question you are curious about and follow short linked sources; each one raises new questions, and the notebook draws how the big question and the smaller ones reshape each other until you choose where to stop.

title: Enduring Questions
subject: library
concept: Turn something you wonder about (Should voting be required?) into a question that reflects an enduring issue such as liberty versus order, then read short expert positions and map where they agree and disagree before choosing supporting questions.

title: Source Portfolio
subject: library
concept: Assemble a portfolio of sources for a contested question that covers a range of views; each source card shows origin, authority and context, and the portfolio scores how well sources corroborate each other and how experts cite and review them.

title: Line Safari
subject: arts
concept: Lines draw themselves across the savanna and the class names each one; then hunt for shapes, mix primaries for a chameleon and draw with line brushes.

title: Art Passport
subject: arts
concept: Visit 14 real artworks from around the world on a map; look closer, talk about what you see and feel, compare pairs and collect passport stamps.

title: Paint Mixer
subject: arts
concept: Mix paint that acts like real pigment to discover secondary and tertiary colors, tints and shades; build the color wheel and mix to match target colors.

title: Near and Far
subject: arts
concept: Rearrange objects in a scene using overlap, size and placement until it looks deep instead of flat.

title: Art Style Match
subject: arts
concept: Match public-domain paintings to their artists and movements; then make a picture in that style.

title: Design Fixer
subject: arts
concept: Fix broken poster layouts by applying balance, contrast and emphasis; before-and-after reveals the difference.

title: Vanishing Point Studio
subject: arts
concept: Draw a hallway or street with one-point perspective guides that snap to the vanishing point.

title: Art Through Time
subject: arts
concept: A scrolling timeline of art movements with public-domain works and the history around them.

title: Gallery Critique
subject: arts
concept: Play a critic, curator and artist debating a work; use the describe-analyze-interpret-judge method.

title: City Skyline Studio
subject: arts
concept: Build a skyline in two-point perspective with adjustable horizon and camera height.

title: Virtual Gallery
subject: arts
concept: Curate a portfolio into a virtual gallery; arrange, title and write artist statements.

title: Beat Buddies
subject: arts
concept: Animal friends march, hop and stomp to a steady beat; the class claps along and freezes when the music stops.

title: Sound Elevator
subject: arts
concept: Play notes on an elevator: up for high, down for low; a volume dial makes the elevator glow loud or soft.

title: Orchestra Zoo
subject: arts
concept: Meet the four instrument families at the zoo and hear 22 real instruments; guess the instrument from its sound and build a zoo band.

title: Note Ninja
subject: arts
concept: Notes fly across a staff; slice them by naming the letter before they reach the end.

title: Melody Maker
subject: arts
concept: Compose melodies on a scale grid where every note sounds good; hear solfege as you play.

title: Song Form Builder
subject: arts
concept: Build songs from A and B sections; arrange AB, ABA and rondo forms and hear the result.

title: Chord Explorer
subject: arts
concept: Build triads and chord progressions on a keyboard; hear why some progressions feel like home.

title: World Music Map
subject: arts
concept: Explore instruments, rhythms and scales from around the world on an interactive map.

title: Band Practice
subject: arts
concept: Play your part in time with a virtual band; the timing meter shows when you rush or drag.

title: Theory Gym
subject: arts
concept: Identify intervals, keys and cadences in puzzles that build from simple to complex.

title: Music History Radio
subject: arts
concept: Tune a radio dial through musical eras from medieval chant to hip hop, using public-domain and original recordings.

title: Beat Lab
subject: arts
concept: A browser studio with a step sequencer, piano roll, song playlist, mixer and a 214-sound library to compose, arrange and produce an original track.

title: Act It Out
subject: arts
concept: The teacher picks a story; kids act it out as the board shows costumes, settings and sound effects.

title: Character Voice Booth
subject: arts
concept: Record the same line in different voices and emotions; play them back and talk about character choices.

title: Stage Blocker
subject: arts
concept: Block a scene on a top-down stage: place actors, lights and set pieces; preview from the audience.

title: Director's Chair
subject: arts
concept: Direct a classic scene with different choices (tone, pacing, setting); see how interpretation changes meaning.

title: Levels and Pathways
subject: arts
concept: An animated dancer stretches, twists and bends at high, middle and low levels, then travels straight, curved and zigzag pathways; the class copies each one, then invents a pathway for the dancer to follow.

title: Dance Pattern Puzzle
subject: arts
concept: Build a dance sequence from move cards to match a pattern (ABAB); perform it at different tempos.

title: Choreography Board
subject: arts
concept: Arrange dancers on a stage and timeline; animate formations and transitions to music.

title: Dance Styles Explorer
subject: arts
concept: Explore dance styles (ballet, hip hop, folk, modern) and write critiques with a vocabulary guide.

title: Frame It
subject: arts
concept: Take virtual photos of a scene; move the camera to practice rule of thirds, leading lines and lighting.

title: Flipbook Studio
subject: arts
concept: Draw frames and play them as a flipbook; experiment with timing and onion skinning.

title: Storyboard Studio
subject: arts
concept: Plan a short film shot by shot: angles, cuts and transitions, with an animatic preview.

title: Brand Builder
subject: arts
concept: Design a logo and brand kit for a fictional business: typography, color and layout with critique prompts.

title: Habit Hero
subject: health-pe
concept: Care for a hero character's day: brushing, washing, sleeping and moving keep the hero's energy up.

title: Lunch Tray Builder
subject: health-pe
concept: Build a balanced lunch tray from the food groups; the plate shows what's missing.

title: Feelings Faces
subject: health-pe
concept: Faces and short scenes on the board; the class names the feeling and suggests a kind response.

title: Safety Street
subject: health-pe
concept: Walk through a neighborhood making safety choices: crossing streets, fire drills and water safety.

title: Label Detective
subject: health-pe
concept: Compare snack labels to find hidden sugar and sodium; solve which snack fits the goal.

title: Body Systems Tour
subject: health-pe
concept: Ride through the body's systems; see how they work together when you run, eat or sleep.

title: Germ Spread Sim
subject: health-pe
concept: See how germs spread in a classroom and how handwashing and covering coughs change the outbreak.

title: Growing Up Q&A
subject: health-pe
concept: A respectful, age-appropriate guide to body changes with an anonymous question box (stored only locally). Teachers configure it to district policy.

title: Pressure Point
subject: health-pe
concept: Navigate realistic peer pressure situations around vaping and alcohol; practice refusal skills.

title: Stress Toolkit
subject: health-pe
concept: Try coping strategies (breathing, grounding, journaling) and track which help; links to support resources.

title: Relationship Spectrum
subject: health-pe
concept: Place short friendship and dating scenarios on a line from healthy to unhealthy; red-flag cards explain each placement, and a 'what you could say' card practices setting the boundary.

title: Screen Week
subject: health-pe
concept: Track a week of pretend screen time; analyze patterns and design a healthier plan.

title: Game Day Fuel
subject: health-pe
concept: Plan a week of meals and workouts that balance energy; the tool flags gaps and extremes.

title: First Aid Responder
subject: health-pe
concept: Respond to emergency scenarios in the right order; practice CPR rhythm with an audio metronome.

title: Health Claim Checker
subject: health-pe
concept: Investigate viral health claims; check sources, studies and motives to decide what's valid.

title: Mind Map
subject: health-pe
concept: Explore mental health conditions, myths vs facts and how to support a friend; links to support resources.

title: Animal Moves
subject: health-pe
concept: An animal appears on the board and the class moves like it (hop like a frog, gallop like a horse).

title: Target Toss
subject: health-pe
concept: Use the board as a target for soft-ball throws; the tool counts hits and coaches form cues.

title: Playbook
subject: health-pe
concept: Design offensive and defensive plays on a game board; test them in a simulated match.

title: Fitness Circuit
subject: health-pe
concept: A projected circuit timer with stations for cardio, strength and flexibility; heart rate check-ins between rounds.

title: Rules Referee
subject: health-pe
concept: Watch play clips and call the right rule; escape the locker room by refereeing correctly.

title: Goal Tracker
subject: health-pe
concept: Set fitness goals and log activity; a growing avatar reflects consistency, not perfection.

title: Fitness Program Designer
subject: health-pe
concept: Design a 6-week program using FITT principles; the tool checks for balance and progression.

title: Captain's Choices
subject: health-pe
concept: Lead a team through wins, losses and conflicts; your choices shape team culture.

title: Robot Dance
subject: computer-science
concept: The class gives a robot step-by-step commands to dance; a wrong step makes it trip and they debug together.

title: Me vs the Counter
subject: computer-science
concept: A ball bounces for ten seconds; half the class tallies the bounces by hand while the computer counts them too; compare the totals and the mistakes, then use the computer's counts to pick the bounciest ball.

title: Secret Keeper
subject: computer-science
concept: Sort information into "OK to share" and "keep private" with a friendly robot guide.

title: Snowy Mail Route
subject: computer-science
concept: The class lays arrow cards to send a mail penguin across a snowy town grid; before it runs, kids trace the route with a finger and predict where it will stop, then run it and fix the card that sent it the wrong way.

title: Spot the AI
subject: computer-science
concept: Everyday scenes play out (a phone unlocking with a face, a map choosing a route, a toy that answers back); the class guesses which ones use AI, and the teacher reveals the pattern each one learned from.

title: Computer Builder
subject: computer-science
concept: Assemble a computer from parts (screen, keyboard, mouse, speakers) and see what each one does.

title: Loop Garden
subject: computer-science
concept: Plant flowers with repeat blocks; fewer blocks earn more stars.

title: Teach the Robot
subject: computer-science
concept: Train a robot to recognize cats vs dogs by giving examples; see how more examples improve it.

title: Input or Output?
subject: computer-science
concept: A tablet, a game controller, a smart speaker and a microwave; the class sorts each part into 'takes in' or 'gives out', then predicts what the gadget does when one input is covered.

title: Traffic Light Coder
subject: computer-science
concept: Program traffic lights with if-then rules so cars and walkers stay safe.

title: Score Keeper
subject: computer-science
concept: Build a simple game and watch variables like score and lives change in real time.

title: Internet Journey
subject: computer-science
concept: Follow a message from your device to a friend's across the internet; protect personal info along the way.

title: Code Tracer
subject: computer-science
concept: Step through code line by line, predicting variable values before they appear.

title: Data Table Builder
subject: computer-science
concept: Collect class data, organize it into a table and make charts to answer a question.

title: Biased Bot
subject: computer-science
concept: Train an AI with skewed examples and see it fail; fix it with better training data.

title: Network Help Desk
subject: computer-science
concept: Families call the help desk because a device won't connect; ask the right questions (wired or wireless? signed in, or just not allowed?) and fix each one.

title: Game Remix
subject: computer-science
concept: Remix a simple game by changing rules, sprites and variables; share it with classmates.

title: Leaf Sorter AI
subject: computer-science
concept: Choose which features (color, edge, shape, size) a classifier may use to sort leaves by tree; see which features separate them and which only add noise, then test it on leaves it has never seen.

title: Data Defenders
subject: computer-science
concept: Protect a school's data from attacks by securing confidentiality, integrity and availability.

title: Design for a Friend
subject: computer-science
concept: Interview a user persona and design an app feature that meets their needs.

title: Chore Flowcharts
subject: computer-science
concept: Build flowcharts for everyday tasks and convert them to pseudocode; test them with inputs.

title: Code Kitchen
subject: computer-science
concept: Write procedures that cook recipes with variables of different types; reuse them to save time.

title: Model Mechanic
subject: computer-science
concept: Tune a model's training data and features to improve accuracy and reduce bias; see the confusion matrix.

title: Misleading Charts
subject: computer-science
concept: Investigate charts that mislead; fix the axes, scales and labels to show the truth.

title: Packet Race
subject: computer-science
concept: Send packets through a network; reroute when routers fail and reassemble the message.

title: Phishing Spotter
subject: computer-science
concept: Spot phishing emails, fake logins and suspicious links in fast rounds; learn the tells.

title: Algorithm Audit
subject: computer-science
concept: Audit a fictional school's algorithm for bias; propose fixes and debate tradeoffs.

title: Sorting Showdown
subject: computer-science
concept: Visualize and race sorting algorithms on different data sets; compare efficiency.

title: API Playground
subject: computer-science
concept: Call mock APIs and build a small app by combining modules and functions.

title: AI Evaluator
subject: computer-science
concept: Test AI-generated outputs for accuracy and bias; evaluate training data and choose the right model type.

title: Simulation Studio
subject: computer-science
concept: Build simulations and clean messy data; visualize results to answer a question.

title: Network Architect
subject: computer-science
concept: Design a school network with routers, switches and firewalls; test traffic and failures.

title: Capture the Flag
subject: computer-science
concept: Beginner-friendly CTF challenges on passwords, encryption and social engineering in a safe sandbox.

title: Data Policy Council
subject: computer-science
concept: Draft a data privacy policy as a council; weigh innovation, privacy and law.

title: Fingerspell Flash
subject: world-languages
concept: Learn the 26 handshapes of the manual alphabet, watch any word or name fingerspelled at your chosen speed, then read fingerspelled words as they speed up.

title: ASL Hello Booth
subject: world-languages
concept: Video greetings by Deaf signers; the class practices together and learns how to get attention appropriately.

title: ASL Number Bingo
subject: world-languages
concept: Bingo with numbers, colors and time signs shown in video.

title: Sign Parameters Lab
subject: world-languages
concept: Change one parameter (handshape, location, movement) and see how the sign's meaning changes.

title: ASL Family Tree
subject: world-languages
concept: Build a family tree and sign each relationship; videos model each sign.

title: Face the Grammar
subject: world-languages
concept: Match facial expressions and non-manual markers to question types and grammar.

title: Classifier Scenes
subject: world-languages
concept: Describe a scene using classifiers to place and move objects in space; compare with Deaf signers' versions.

title: Deaf Culture Explorer
subject: world-languages
concept: Explore Deaf history, culture and community voices; content developed with Deaf educators.

title: ASL Story Theater
subject: world-languages
concept: Record or plan an ASL story with role shift; watch Deaf storytellers for models.

title: Hola Hallway
subject: world-languages
concept: Greet animated classmates in Spanish as they walk past; the class chooses the right greeting for each time of day.

title: Calendario Vivo
subject: world-languages
concept: An interactive calendar in Spanish; click days, weather and colors to hear and practice.

title: Mi Casa
subject: world-languages
concept: Explore a house and family in Spanish; tap objects and people to hear names.

title: Mi Día
subject: world-languages
concept: Build your daily routine timeline in Spanish with reflexive verbs and times.

title: El Restaurante
subject: world-languages
concept: Order food in a Spanish-speaking restaurant; practice likes, dislikes and polite requests.

title: Verb Conjugation Race
subject: world-languages
concept: Race through conjugations of regular and irregular verbs; each correct answer speeds up your car.

title: Ciudad Perdida
subject: world-languages
concept: Navigate a Spanish-speaking city using directions; ask for and give directions in Spanish.

title: Detective del Pasado
subject: world-languages
concept: Solve a mystery by telling what happened with the preterite and imperfect.

title: Mundo Hispano
subject: world-languages
concept: Explore Spanish-speaking countries' traditions, food and music on an interactive map.

title: Consejero
subject: world-languages
concept: Give advice and opinions in Spanish using the subjunctive; respond to friends' problems.

title: Debate en Español
subject: world-languages
concept: Debate current events in Spanish using structured arguments and counterarguments.

title: Career Cluster Explorer
subject: cte
concept: Explore the 14 career clusters with videos, job examples and pathways.

title: Career Match Quiz
subject: cte
concept: Answer questions about interests and strengths; see matching careers and what they involve.

title: Workplace Scenarios
subject: cte
concept: Navigate workplace situations: teamwork, communication and professionalism.

title: Path Planner
subject: cte
concept: Compare college, apprenticeships, certificates and military paths; plan a route to a goal.

title: Interview Simulator
subject: cte
concept: Practice job interviews with common questions; get feedback on answers.

title: Startup Booth
subject: cte
concept: Launch a business: plan, budget, market and pitch to investors.

title: Prototype Lab
subject: cte
concept: Design, prototype and test a product; iterate based on test results.

title: Hospital Shift
subject: cte
concept: Spend a shift in a hospital in different roles; learn medical terms and career paths.

title: Paycheck Decoder
subject: cte
concept: Decode a paycheck: gross pay, taxes, deductions and benefits.

title: First Apartment Budget
subject: cte
concept: Budget for your first apartment; balance rent, food, transport and fun.

title: Compound Interest Head Start
subject: cte
concept: Two savers put in the same $50 a month, one from age 16 and one from 26; a stacked bar splits each year into deposits, interest and interest on interest. Change the rate or how often it compounds, then find the rule of 72. A plain savings account at a fixed rate, so no market returns (market-time-machine) and no doubling-penny sequences (savings-plan).

title: The Credit Card Diaries
subject: cte
concept: Live four years of a young adult's life making card, loan and phone-plan choices; the credit score and debt follow every decision.

title: Market Time Machine
subject: cte
concept: Invest across asset types using historical index data; learn about risk, diversification and time. Educational only, no picks or advice.

title: Covered: Insurance Claims
subject: cte
concept: Compare three renters quotes, trade the monthly premium against the deductible and see what each costs in a quiet, theft or fire year; then catch fake 'claim refund' texts using your own policy page.

title: Feelings Weather Report
subject: sel
concept: Kids report their feelings as weather (sunny, stormy); the class learns feeling words together.

title: Calm Corner
subject: sel
concept: Animated calm-down tools: breathing balloons, counting and stretching, led by the teacher.

title: Walk in Their Shoes
subject: sel
concept: Experience a story from different characters' perspectives; discuss feelings and needs.

title: Comeback Club
subject: sel
concept: Train a brain character through challenges; practice and comebacks level it up and goals unlock new areas.

title: Conflict Coach
subject: sel
concept: Practice resolving conflicts with peers using I-statements and active listening.

title: Decision Tree
subject: sel
concept: Map decisions and consequences for real-life scenarios; weigh options and outcomes.

title: Resilience Map
subject: sel
concept: Explore stress responses and resilience strategies; build a personal plan with resources.

title: Community Project Planner
subject: sel
concept: Plan and lead a community service project; manage team, time and resources.

title: Attic Gadget Box
subject: computer-science
concept: The class opens a grandparent's attic box (a rotary phone, a paper map, a cassette player) and slides each gadget to the device that does its job today, then meets the people, from many places and abilities, who designed the new one to solve a problem.

title: Question Jar
subject: computer-science
concept: The class pulls questions from a jar and sorts them: can we find out by counting, measuring or asking, or is it an opinion? Then they pick how to collect, numbers or words, see who the plan leaves out, and reword the question.

title: Who Uses This Device?
subject: computer-science
concept: The class visits a street fair of grown-ups at work (a baker, a vet, a bus driver, an artist, a coach) and taps each one to see the device they use and what it helps them do; second graders match a hobby to a computing job.

title: Tablet Buddy
subject: computer-science
concept: The class guides a small classroom pet through a school day with the shared class tablet, choosing at each turn (gentle hands, headphones, its own login, a break after a long video), and sees how each choice helps or hurts the pet and its friends.

title: Line Leader Picker
subject: computer-science
concept: The class writes the rule for choosing the line leader (ABC order, draw a name, draw and put it back, take turns around the circle), runs a pretend month of school days, and counts who led often and who never got a turn.

title: Morning Meeting Board
subject: computer-science
concept: The class reads the picture signs on the morning board (weather, lunch choice, a quiet hand), names each box, and predicts which values will change by lunch, by tomorrow or never; a time slider jumps ahead and reveals the board.

title: Tap-to-Start Puppets
subject: computer-science
concept: Puppets on a little stage each hold a short program that starts when you tap them; the class says what each block will make happen, watches it run, and second graders retell how the show was built and who helped.

title: Inventors Hall
subject: computer-science
concept: Students walk an inventors' hall and place each exhibit on a timeline (a punch-card loom, an early compiler, a talking calculator, a game cartridge), reading what the old way could not do, why people built the new one and whose ideas were left out.

title: Job Shadow Day
subject: computer-science
concept: Students shadow four workers through a day (a vet, a farmer, an animator, a bus dispatcher), choose how each uses a computer at key moments, see how they learned a new tool, and watch them share work with a teammate to solve the day's problem.

title: Family Tech Vote
subject: computer-science
concept: A family votes on a new gadget (a smart speaker, a fitness watch, a doorbell camera); students take each family member's seat, flip cards for what it helps, what data it collects, what it costs the planet and who it leaves out, then explain the choice.

title: Fair Survey Kit
subject: computer-science
concept: Students plan a survey about a new playground (who to ask, number or word answers, an opt-out box), then the answers arrive with blanks, misspellings and an age of 400, and they check, fix and sort them in a table before counting.

title: Marble Ramp Trials
subject: computer-science
concept: Students time a marble down a cardboard ramp again and again; the times never match, so they hunt for causes (a late tap, a bump, a typo) and mark outliers, then change the ramp's height and surface to see how two attributes work together.

title: Team Code Relay
subject: computer-science
concept: Two or three students each build one part of a small game (movement, score, sound) on their own side of the screen, then snap the parts together; when the joined game breaks, they read each part, leave comments, compare two fixes and trade feedback.

title: Adventure Outline Cards
subject: computer-science
concept: Students outline a choose-your-own-adventure as numbered steps with a repeat and an if-then fork, written in words at grade 4 and redrawn as an index-card diagram with a coin counter at grade 5; a reader token walks every path to find dead ends.

title: Three Route Rules
subject: computer-science
concept: A walking app can pick routes three ways (fastest, fewest street crossings, no stairs); students run each rule for four travelers, a kid, a wheelchair user, a parent with a stroller and a jogger, and see who each rule helps and who it lets down.

title: Inside the Keypress
subject: computer-science
concept: Press a key or snap a photo and follow the signal from keyboard to memory to the app's instructions to the screen; swap the app (drawing, typing, a game) to see the same hardware do a new job, then find the step that left the screen blank.

title: Metadata X-Ray
subject: computer-science
concept: Students flip a phone photo, a step-tracker log and a school app record to reveal their metadata (time, place, device), turn dials for precision and how often data is recorded, and decide who should keep which details and where that data lives.

title: Lunch Survey Cleanup
subject: computer-science
concept: A school lunch survey arrives with blanks, mixed spellings and doubled rows; students pick a fix for each problem (drop, reformat or keep), watch the results and the students left out of the data change, then write a short report on their choices and limits.

title: Accessibility Test Team
subject: computer-science
concept: A team of three takes turns testing a club sign-up app as different users (a screen reader user, a student new to English, someone with a shaky hand), logs what failed, agrees on fixes with every voice counted, and retests to see who it now serves.

title: County Connection Grant
subject: computer-science
concept: Students spend a grant to get a rural county online, matching each household (a farm family, a grandparent, a student, the library) to a device and a connection by need, cost and battery; then a new telehealth app shows whose language, bandwidth or device it leaves out.

title: AI Fit Check
subject: computer-science
concept: Students sort a stack of jobs (total a bill, enforce game rules, suggest a song, group lost-and-found photos) into steps, rules or a data-driven model, then run a pretend AI helper on two of them, check its answers and weigh its energy cost.

title: AI Code Inspector
subject: computer-science
concept: An AI helper writes a quiz program that looks right; students look up each function in the reference docs (two do not exist), run test inputs, log every change in a fix log, and add credits for the AI help and a borrowed sound.

title: Industry Device Tour
subject: computer-science
concept: Students tour a dairy farm, a hospital imaging room and a car plant, open each machine to see its input, processing, storage and output, then match each worker's problem to the thinking move they use: break it down, spot a pattern or leave out details.

title: Eras of Computing
subject: computer-science
concept: Students place inventors, communities, companies and governments on a timeline of computing eras, trace one past technology's intended and surprise effects (jobs, privacy, e-waste), then use those lessons to argue for or against delivery drones in their own town.

title: Emerging Tech Pitch
subject: computer-science
concept: Students pick a local problem (smoke alerts, late buses, library access), compare how an emerging technology (drones, on-device AI, satellite internet) works against the established fix, sketch a concept, and run an impact check on energy, cost and who gets left out.

title: Cloud Through Time
subject: computer-science
concept: Students follow one technology, the data center, from room-sized mainframes to today's AI server farms, link each step to the social and economic forces behind it, and tag each era with its energy and water use and the towns and workers who carry the cost.

title: Dice in the Chatbot
subject: computer-science
concept: Students send the same prompt to a rule-based chatbot and to a tiny next-word predictor, turn the randomness dial and watch the answers change, then sort claims about understanding, feeling and responsibility into a debate backed by what they measured.

title: Pull Request Review
subject: computer-science
concept: Students review an AI-written pull request for a club website: run it against the requirements and tests, find the hidden bug and the license clash in a pasted snippet, then approve it, request changes or rewrite it with proper credit.

title: Sprint Board
subject: computer-science
concept: A team of four builds a bus-alert app for a client: they write a design doc and assign roles on a sprint board, then user tests and a spec checklist return issues, and each sprint they choose fixes weighing correctness, accessibility and the client's values.

title: Catalog Column Rules
subject: computer-science
concept: Students write the data dictionary for a library's checkout dataset (name, type, allowed values, links between columns), then try three ways to check new rows (rules at entry, a cleaning script, a librarian's review) and compare what each catches and misses.

title: Computing Team Stories
subject: computer-science
concept: Students pick their interests and goals, then meet five computing teams (a game studio, a public health data team, a climate modeling group, a newsroom graphics desk, a prosthetics startup), see how each mix of people cracked one problem, and sketch their own next steps.

title: Coin Cell Greenhouse
subject: computer-science
concept: Students program a simulated microcontroller to water a greenhouse on a coin battery; its slow sensor, 2 KB of memory and sleep mode set hard limits, so they refactor the loop into procedures and smarter control flow until it lasts a month.

title: Snow Season Prices
subject: cte
concept: Run the shops of a ski town through one winter: a big snow, a new rental shop and hotels short of workers move the prices of lift tickets, rentals and wages; students play buyers and sellers and explain each change.

title: Economy Checkup
subject: cte
concept: Read real unemployment, inflation and output data from the last 30 years the way a doctor reads a chart, then see how each high-inflation or job-loss year hit four neighbors differently: a saver, a borrower, a retiree and a job seeker.

title: Interest Rate Dial
subject: cte
concept: Turn one interest rate dial and watch four people respond: a saver's account grows faster or slower, a car buyer's payment changes, a credit card balance swells, and a cafe owner decides whether to borrow to expand.

title: Startup Shares
subject: cte
concept: Spread a pretend $1,000 across five made-up young companies with new ideas, or a basket of all of them, and fast-forward ten years: some inventions flop, some take off, and the basket shows how spreading out changes risk.

title: E-Bike Buyer
subject: cte
concept: Choose an e-bike from ads, reviews and a friend's advice, add up the true cost (charger, lock, helmet, repairs), then decide on a warranty, insurance or a repair fund as crashes, thefts and flat tires come up.

title: Weekend Drawing Share
subject: arts
concept: Children draw something that really happened to them, then a partner taps question cards (What is happening here? Why that color?) and the artist adds one new detail; the class finds out that art can tell their own story.

title: Hallway Art Museum
subject: arts
concept: The class turns a school hallway into a museum: pick favorite works from a pile of kid art and say why, frame and label each one, hang them at kid eye level, then tour the finished show as visitors.

title: Traveling Art Show
subject: arts
concept: Get six student artworks ready for a show at the town library: choose works that fit the theme with a checklist, pack and hang each so chalk will not smudge or clay crack, write labels, and compare the library with a museum.

title: Place Mood Makeover
subject: arts
concept: Pick a familiar place like a bus stop or the lunchroom, choose a mood, then change its colors, light and details; a partner guesses the mood and names the clues, and the artist revises until the mood reads.

title: School Wall Mural
subject: arts
concept: The class plans a mural for the school wall facing the street: gather ideas about what the community cares about, judge sketches against agreed criteria, lay out the wall for people walking by, and argue for the final design.

title: Sketchbook Process Journal
subject: arts
concept: Start from a present-day issue and an older art tradition, then log each step from thumbnail to finished plan; the journal shows how research, culture and history changed the idea and where the artist's own voice came in.

title: Parade and Bedtime Music
subject: arts
concept: Listen to short tunes and drag each one to the moment it fits: bedtime, a parade, a birthday, a rainy day; the class names the clue (soft, fast, bouncy), then votes on a favorite and says why.

title: Name Song Practice
subject: arts
concept: Children make a short song from their name and a favorite thing, sing it into the tool, listen back, pick one fix a friend suggests, and then perform the new version with expression for the class.

title: Recorder Concert Rehearsal
subject: arts
concept: A recorder group rehearses for the spring concert: the class listens to each take, marks it on a checklist (together, in tune, steady tempo), gives the group one note to fix, and hears the next take improve before the show.

title: Cartoon Soundtrack Mixer
subject: arts
concept: Score a silent cartoon: pick music and sound effects for each scene, change the tempo and loudness to fit the mood, then play it back and find out how the same pictures feel different with new music.

title: Folk Song Arranger
subject: arts
concept: Take a public-domain folk tune and arrange it for a small band: choose instruments, add an intro and a new section, get peer feedback, revise, and explain how the arrangement suits the concert where it will be played.

title: Cover Version Review
subject: arts
concept: Hear two performances of the same song on a student radio show, mark what each performer changed (tempo, dynamics, instruments), explain what each version is trying to say, and write a short review backed by criteria.

title: Recital Practice Plan
subject: arts
concept: Plan a ten-minute recital: choose pieces that suit the venue and audience, map a practice schedule for the hardest passages, score recorded takes on a rubric you build, and explain why the set means something to you.

title: Puppet Show Feelings
subject: arts
concept: Watch a short puppet scene, then pause it to say how each puppet feels and how you can tell, pick the ending you liked best, and find one way a puppet is like you.

title: Moon Base Drama
subject: arts
concept: The teacher plays the base commander and the class becomes the crew of a moon base: choose a prop that shows your job, ask and answer questions in role, and use real facts about the moon to solve the crew's problem.

title: Neighborhood Issue Play
subject: arts
concept: Small groups invent a short play about a real neighborhood problem, like a closed park or a new kid on the block: build the characters, sketch the set and costumes, rehearse, and share the play with the class.

title: Audience Talkback
subject: arts
concept: Watch two versions of the same short scene with different costumes, lights and voices; the class rates each against a group checklist, then explains which worked better using their own experiences as evidence.

title: Three Viewpoints Scene
subject: arts
concept: Devise a short scene about a school issue from three characters' viewpoints: draw perspective cards, draft the beats, run the scene, take in a partner's idea, tighten the pacing, and perform it for the class.

title: Scene Staging Comparison
subject: arts
concept: Compare two productions of the same scene from a public-domain play, record your reactions next to a classmate's, find how culture and choices shaped each one, and back your verdict with evidence from the staging.

title: Stage Lighting Plot
subject: arts
concept: Light a scene from a play: research its time and place, hang and aim lights, pick colors and cues, run the scene, and revise until the light supports the story and its emotional turns.

title: Monologue Rehearsal
subject: arts
concept: Pick a monologue, answer the given circumstances (where am I, what do I want, what is in my way), try vocal and physical choices in rehearsal, and perform it for a chosen audience while connecting it to your own beliefs.

title: Feeling Scarf Dance
subject: arts
concept: Pick a feeling card, then dance it with a scarf in three parts, a beginning, a middle and an end; half the class dances while the other half watches, and everyone names a time they felt that way.

title: Family Dance Night
subject: arts
concept: At family dance night in the school gym, families teach a dance from home: watch the animated dancers, copy a move and describe it with dance words, pick a favorite part, and find out how each dance connects to the people and place it comes from.

title: Poem to Movement
subject: arts
concept: Pick a poem, painting or sound as a starting idea, build a short movement phrase from it, draw its pathway as a floor map, then revise after a partner's feedback and compare the dance's idea to your own life.

title: Recital Stage Directions
subject: arts
concept: Place dancers using upstage, downstage, stage left and stage right, add costumes and lights for a recital, then switch to an audience seat to read the dance's clues, find its main idea and compare two styles.

title: Dancers on Tour
subject: arts
concept: A dance company tours a gym, a park and a theater; adapt spacing, timing and focus to each venue, apply the choreographer's notes after each show, and keep the dancers safe with warm-ups and good technique.

title: Dance Hall Decades
subject: arts
concept: Move through social dances from different decades and communities, spot the patterns in each, explain what the moves say about their time and people, judge them with criteria, and relate one to your own movement preferences.

title: Choreography for a Cause
subject: arts
concept: Research an issue that matters to you, generate movement from what you find, structure a dance with a clear form, revise it with feedback from viewers, and explain how the piece connects to your own experiences.

title: Museum Courtyard Performance
subject: arts
concept: Produce a dance concert in a museum courtyard: adapt the choreography to the space, plan lighting, sound and audience flow, schedule rehearsals that build technique safely, and lead the crew to opening night.

title: Sound and Picture Book
subject: arts
concept: Children plan a three-page story with picture cards, draw or snap a picture for each page, record a sound for each one, and put the pages in order; playing it back shows how pictures and sounds work together.

title: Field Trip Slideshow
subject: arts
concept: The class makes a slideshow about a shared trip: each child takes a crew job (camera, sound, speaker) and picks a favorite memory to include, then the class presents the slideshow to visitors and shares how it felt.

title: Cereal Ad Questions
subject: arts
concept: Watch silly made-up cereal ads, find the parts (pictures, music, words), say what each ad wants you to think, pick what you would change, and talk about where ads show up in everyday life and how to use screens safely.

title: Stop-Motion Clay Shoot
subject: arts
concept: Plan a short stop-motion scene on a storyboard, pose clay figures frame by frame, fix jumpy movement and timing, then screen the scene for the class and note what to improve next time.

title: Toy Ad Reality Check
subject: arts
concept: Pause a made-up toy commercial to find the camera tricks, music and words that make the toy look bigger and better, decide what the ad wants you to believe, and rate it against what the toy really does.

title: Morning Show Crew
subject: arts
concept: Run the school's morning show crew: tell one story as a video segment, a poster and a short post, decide which format reaches which audience, and plan the release around topics students care about.

title: Viral Video Breakdown
subject: arts
concept: Take apart a made-up viral video shot by shot: how the framing, music and captions steer viewers, what the maker wanted, how the comments read it, and what copyright and fairness questions come up when it is reposted.

title: Mini Documentary Crew
subject: arts
concept: Lead a crew making a five-minute documentary about a local story: combine interviews, footage and music, assign roles and keep the shoot on schedule, test cuts with viewers, and plan where it premieres.

title: Weekend Substance Choices
subject: health-pe
concept: Follow a weekend with friends where alcohol, vapes and cannabis edibles show up: choose what to say and do, see how each choice affects the body, the law and friendships, and practice getting help for a friend in trouble.

title: Recess Upstander
subject: health-pe
concept: At recess someone is left out, teased or pushed; practice upstander moves (say stop, help the target walk away, get an adult), see how the bystanders react, and learn to tell bullying apart from an ordinary conflict.

title: Worry Size Sorter
subject: health-pe
concept: Sort everyday worries into small, medium and big, try a coping tool for each, find out that big worries go to a trusted adult, and set a one-week coping goal to check off each day.

title: Safety Sweep House
subject: health-pe
concept: Search a house room by room for hazards: medicine within reach, mixed cleaners, a blocked smoke alarm, a stranger asking for an address in a game chat; choose the safe action for each and see what could happen otherwise.

title: Fridge Goal Chart
subject: health-pe
concept: Pick one health goal, like more water or an earlier bedtime, put it on the fridge chart, see what helps and what gets in the way (a TV ad, a busy night), name who can help, and add a star each day.

title: Parachute Teamwork
subject: health-pe
concept: The class plays parachute games on the board and in the room: take turns, follow the leader's calls, cheer for others, and notice how a fast heartbeat and big smiles show that moving is good for you.

title: Scarf Juggling Ladder
subject: health-pe
concept: Learn scarf juggling one rung at a time, from one scarf to two to three; check each rung against cue cards, log practice tries, and find out that steady practice beats giving up after a drop.

title: Partner Skill Coach
subject: health-pe
concept: Watch a partner throw, kick or shoot, compare the move to cue cards, give one helpful tip in a kind way, then switch roles; the class learns to analyze a skill and to coach each other respectfully.

title: Friend Moves Practice
subject: sel
concept: Practice friend moves with classroom characters: ask to join a game, share the blocks, take turns, and fix a small problem with a sorry; the class sees how each move changes the friend's face.

title: First Impressions Check
subject: sel
concept: Meet strangers on a city bus, make a snap guess about each one, then reveal more of their story; notice which guesses came from your own biases and how a new perspective changes the picture.

title: Hundred Hop
subject: math
concept: A frog hops along a giant 1-100 path on the projector; the class counts aloud by ones or tens and calls out where it lands before the teacher reveals.

title: Sheep Count
subject: math
concept: Sheep wander into a pen one at a time; kids touch-count along with the teacher, then guess how many are hiding when the barn door closes.

title: Snack Scale
subject: math
concept: A seesaw takes piles of cartoon snacks; whichever side has more tips down, and kids predict which way before the teacher lets go.

title: Bus Stop
subject: math
concept: A school bus picks up and drops off riders at each stop; the class tells the addition or subtraction story out loud.

title: Ten Frame Spillover
subject: math
concept: Fill a ten frame, then spill the extras onto a second; the number name and "ten and some more" build as you go.

title: Who Wins?
subject: math
concept: Two animals face off on length, weight or height; kids vote with thumbs, then the measuring tape or scale settles it.

title: Toy Box Sort
subject: math
