concept: Dump a toy box and sort by color, shape or size; the tool counts each pile and builds a tiny picture graph.

title: Shape Spy
subject: math
concept: Photos of a playground, kitchen and street hide circles, squares and cubes; tap to reveal outlines and names.

title: Pattern Block Pond
subject: math
concept: Snap pattern blocks together to fill a lily pad outline; the tool celebrates when two triangles make a rhombus.

title: Story Problem Theater
subject: math
concept: Short animated stories pause at the question; students act out the problem with counters before choosing the number sentence.

title: Make Ten Machine
subject: math
concept: Pairs of numbers roll in on a conveyor; slide counters across to make a ten and watch the harder fact turn easy.

title: Balance the Beam
subject: math
concept: A balance scale with numbers on both sides; find the missing weight so it levels. Kills the "equals means the answer comes next" myth.

title: Number Path Rescue
subject: math
concept: Missing tiles on a 120 chart; fill them before the river rises. Patterns in the chart make it faster.

title: Crayon Boxes
subject: math
concept: Pack the class's loose crayons into boxes of ten for every table; say how many boxes and loose crayons, then compare two classrooms' supplies with >, = and <.

title: Elevator Hundred
subject: math
concept: An elevator moves up by tens and floors by ones in a hundred-chart building; ride it to solve sums.

title: Paperclip Ruler
subject: math
concept: Measure classroom objects with paperclips, cubes or shoes; compare results and discover why same-size units matter.

title: Clock Shop
subject: math
concept: Drag the hands of a big friendly clock and watch the digital clock and the day's sky change with them.

title: Class Poll
subject: math
concept: The class votes on favorite pets or snacks; tallies turn into a picture graph live on the board for discussion.

title: Pizza Party
subject: math
concept: Cut pizzas and sandwiches so friends get fair shares; uneven cuts get a funny complaint from a guest.

title: Lost and Found
subject: math
concept: Two-step clues about what came in and went out of the lost and found each day ('14 mittens, 6 picked up, 5 more found') point to the box that holds the missing toy.

title: Fact Rally
subject: math
concept: Volley facts back and forth with a tennis bot; strategies (doubles, near doubles, make ten) unlock power shots.

title: Marching Band
subject: math
concept: Line up band members in rows; can everyone have a partner? Arrays reveal odd and even and repeated addition.

title: Place Value Vault
subject: math
concept: Crack three-digit vault codes from clues like "7 tens, 2 hundreds, 0 ones." Teams race the alarm.

title: Jump Line
subject: math
concept: An open number line where you make your own jumps; compare different students' paths to the same answer.

title: Estimation Station
subject: math
concept: Estimate lengths in inches or centimeters, then measure with an on-screen ruler; closeness earns points.

title: Corner Store
subject: math
concept: Run a snack stand: count coins, make change and close by 3:45 when the bell rings.

title: Lunch Line Data
subject: math
concept: Real-feeling cafeteria data; build bar graphs and line plots and answer "how many more?" questions.

title: Garden Grid
subject: math
concept: Partition a garden bed into equal rows and columns of plants; count the squares to plan the planting.

title: Equal Groups Zoo
subject: math
concept: Feed zoo animals equal groups; the tool shows the same picture as an array, a skip-count and an equation.

title: Multiplication Dungeon
subject: math
concept: A retro dungeon crawl where each door is a fact; facts you miss come back as tougher monsters until mastered.

title: Pattern Painter
subject: math
concept: Color the multiplication table to make patterns pop (every even product, every multiple of 5, the square numbers), predict the next colored square and explain the rule in one sentence, then use a pattern to crack a two-step word problem.

title: Roller Coaster Rounding
subject: math
concept: A coaster car rolls to the nearest ten or hundred hill; see why 45 rolls up.

title: Fraction Trail
subject: math
concept: Hike a trail marked in fractions; place campsites at 3/4 or 2/2 and discover equivalent points.

title: Kitchen Lab
subject: math
concept: Measure liquids and weigh ingredients for recipes while a timer runs; plan elapsed time so dinner is ready at 6.

title: Graph Glow-Up
subject: math
concept: Redesign a crowded picture graph with a better scale; compare which version tells the story clearly.

title: Tile the Floor
subject: math
concept: Cover rooms with square tiles, then shortcut with rows times columns. Odd-shaped rooms split into rectangles.

title: Fence Builder
subject: math
concept: Build a dog pen with a fixed amount of fencing; find the shape with the most room. Area vs perimeter, felt.

title: Shape Family Tree
subject: math
concept: Sort quadrilaterals into a family tree; argue whether a square belongs with rectangles.

title: Growth Spurt
subject: math
concept: Compare animals and plants: "times as tall" vs "taller by." Sliders show the difference between additive and multiplicative.

title: Prime Garden
subject: math
concept: Plant numbers as rectangular gardens; primes only grow in a single row. Find every shape for 36.

title: Rule Machine
subject: math
concept: Numbers go in, numbers come out; guess the rule, then build one for classmates to crack.

title: Stadium Count
subject: math
concept: Zoom from one seat to a full stadium to a city; see thousands and hundred-thousands as real crowds.

title: Area Model Builder
subject: math
concept: Split big multiplications into rectangles you can actually compute, then put them back together.

title: Fraction Wall Duel
subject: math
concept: A two-player card game on a fraction wall: play a fraction bigger than your opponent's, or an equal one to steal.

title: Recipe Scaler
subject: math
concept: Scale a family recipe up for the whole class party: multiply each fraction of a cup by the number of batches and watch the measuring cups fill. No shop to run and no customers, so it no longer sits beside grocery-run and the pizza shop.

title: Money and Meters
subject: math
concept: Tenths and hundredths shown three ways: dimes and pennies, meter sticks, and grids. Change one and the others follow.

title: Unit Ladder
subject: math
concept: Climb a conversion ladder (feet to inches, kilograms to grams) against the clock with a conversion table that unlocks as you go.

title: Skate Park Angles
subject: math
concept: Design ramps and turns with a protractor; the skater can only land certain angles.

title: Mirror Studio
subject: math
concept: Draw half a design and the mirror line finishes it; hunt for lines of symmetry in flags and logos.

title: Expression Escape
subject: math
concept: Each lock takes an expression; parentheses move to make the right code. Teams decide where to put them.

title: Two Rule Race
subject: math
concept: Two snails follow different rules; plot their positions and see their relationship on the coordinate grid.

title: Powers of Ten Zoom
subject: math
concept: Zoom from a galaxy to an atom by powers of ten; the decimal point slides as you go.

title: Grocery Run
subject: math
concept: Plan a party on a budget; multiply prices, divide bulk packs and check the receipt.

title: Fraction Kitchen
subject: math
concept: Combine measuring cups of different sizes to hit exact amounts; find common denominators to pour without spilling.

title: Shrink Ray
subject: math
concept: Multiply by a fraction and the shrink ray scales the picture; multiply by more than one and it grows.

title: Seed Sprout Data
subject: math
concept: Measure fractional heights of seedlings over days, plot them, and redistribute water evenly.

title: Box Packer
subject: math
concept: Pack cubes into shipping boxes; find the volume formula by watching layers stack.

title: Sea Search Grid
subject: math
concept: Hide boats on the first quadrant and call coordinates to find a partner's; each miss tells you how far off you were.

title: Shape Courtroom
subject: math
concept: Put a shape on trial: is a square a rhombus? Present the evidence (sides and angles) to the jury.

title: Smoothie Lab
subject: math
concept: Mix fruit in ratios and taste-test (the tool reacts); find recipes that taste the same at bigger sizes.

title: How Many Fit?
subject: math
concept: Drag fraction bars into a container to see how many 3/4s fit in 2 1/2. Division as measuring.

title: Factor Forge
subject: math
concept: Smash numbers into prime factors; matching factors between two numbers forge their GCF and LCM.

title: Deep Sea Dive
subject: math
concept: A diver and a bird share a vertical number line; plot positions above and below sea level and compare distances.

title: Expression Garden
subject: math
concept: Grow expressions with algebra tiles; equivalent gardens look different but hold the same plants.

title: Balance Puzzle
subject: math
concept: Mystery bags on a balance; remove the same weight from both sides to find what's inside.

title: Lemonade Stand
subject: math
concept: Change temperature and price; watch sales respond in a table, graph and equation all at once.

title: Net Folder
subject: math
concept: Unfold boxes and pyramids into nets, find the area of each face, then fold them back up.

title: Question Lab
subject: math
concept: Sort questions as statistical or not ("How tall am I?" vs "How tall are 6th graders?") and design your own survey.

title: Box Plot Builder
subject: math
concept: Real sports and weather data; drag points and watch mean, median and box plot react. Outliers get dramatic.

title: Tax and Tip
subject: math
concept: Run a diner register: tips, tax and discounts. Spot the constant of proportionality in every receipt.

title: Hot Air and Sandbags
subject: math
concept: Add hot air (positives) and sandbags (negatives) to a balloon; removing a sandbag goes up. Signed rules become obvious.

title: Expression Match
subject: math
concept: Memory-style card game: match expressions that are equivalent but written differently.

title: Phone Plan Showdown
subject: math
concept: Compare two phone plans as a salesperson and a skeptical customer; equations prove which is cheaper and when.

title: Blueprint Studio
subject: math
concept: Design a dream bedroom on a scale floor plan; the 3D preview shows whether the bed actually fits.

title: Big Wheel, Small Wheel
subject: math
concept: Settle classic round-object arguments (one big trampoline or two small ones? a 26-inch bike wheel or a 20-inch?) by measuring circumference and area.

title: Jellybean Jar
subject: math
concept: Draw random samples from a giant jar to estimate the color mix; bigger samples get closer to the truth.

title: Carnival Odds
subject: math
concept: Spin wheels and roll dice thousands of times; compare theoretical odds to the experiment. Are the carnival games fair?

title: Square Root Hunt
subject: math
concept: Squeeze the square root of 2 between closer and closer decimals on a zooming number line.

title: Size of Everything
subject: math
concept: From a virus to the Milky Way: compare sizes in scientific notation on a slider through scales.

title: Ski Slope Designer
subject: math
concept: Design ski runs by slope; too steep crashes, too flat stalls. Rise over run becomes a feel.

title: Two Trains
subject: math
concept: Two trains, two equations, one graph; drag speeds and start times to see where (and if) they meet.

title: Function Machine Factory
subject: math
concept: Build machines that turn inputs into outputs; a broken machine gives two outputs for one input and the factory rejects it.

title: Story Graphs
subject: math
concept: Match stories ("I ran, then stopped for water") to the graphs that tell them, then draw your own.

title: Dance Floor Moves
subject: math
concept: Choreograph a shape through slides, flips, turns and dilations to music; replay the routine as a sequence of rules.

title: Square Slicer
subject: math
concept: Cut the two small squares and rearrange the pieces to fill the big one; then use it to find shortcuts across a park.

title: Snow Globe Maker
subject: math
concept: Design snow globes, cone-shaped tree ornaments and cylinder bases; volume decides how much water and glitter each needs and what each costs to make.

title: Data Detective
subject: math
concept: Real data (shoe size vs height, study time vs score); fit a line, spot outliers, read a two-way table.

title: Exponent Rule Builder
subject: math
concept: Unlock exponent rules by experimenting with patterns, then prove why a 1/2 power is a square root.

title: Unit Sense
subject: math
concept: Real headlines with impossible numbers; use dimensional analysis to find which claims fall apart.

title: Algebra Tile Studio
subject: math
concept: Factor and complete the square with algebra tiles; watch the rectangle and the expression change together.

title: Polynomials as Numbers
subject: math
concept: Set x = 10 and watch every polynomial become an ordinary number; multiplying polynomials turns into long multiplication without carrying, and like terms line up like place-value columns.

title: Model My World
subject: math
concept: Pick a real situation (phone data, gym fees, savings) and write the equation that predicts it; the tool checks it against data.

title: Equation Golf
subject: math
concept: Solve equations in as few legal moves as possible; par scores reward elegant solutions.

title: Intersection Quest
subject: math
concept: Find where two lines cross three ways (graph, substitution, elimination) and race your own best time.

title: Graph Story Lab
subject: math
concept: Explore real graphs (a day of temperatures, a roller coaster) and label domain, range, max and intervals.

title: Which Model Wins?
subject: math
concept: Real data sets (viral videos, braking distance, savings): fit linear, quadratic and exponential models and pick the best.

title: Launch Pad
subject: math
concept: Launch a projectile and see its quadratic; the roots are where it lands. Solve to aim for targets.

title: Correlation Guessing Game
subject: math
concept: Guess the correlation of a scatter plot; residual plots expose the trick ones.

title: Rigid Motion Twins
subject: math
concept: Each level shows a shape and its twin; map one onto the other with the fewest rigid motions, then write the sequence as the proof that they are congruent.

title: Proof Tower
subject: math
concept: Drag statements and reasons into a proof that holds up; a compass-and-straightedge sandbox handles constructions.

title: Shadow Measure
subject: math
concept: Measure a flagpole with its shadow and a meter stick using similar triangles, then check with the real height.

title: Ramp and Roof
subject: math
concept: Design accessible ramps and roof pitches that meet code using sine, cosine and tangent.

title: Circle Theorem Explorer
subject: math
concept: Drag points around circles and watch inscribed angles, chords and tangents keep their relationships.

title: Coordinate Proof Lab
subject: math
concept: Place shapes on the grid and prove they're parallelograms or rectangles with slopes and distances.

title: Slice and Stack
subject: math
concept: Slice 3D solids with a moving plane and see the cross sections; spin shapes to make solids of rotation.

title: Packaging Challenge
subject: math
concept: Design a can or box that holds a given volume with the least material; compare against real products.

title: Medical Test Paradox
subject: math
concept: Run a population through a disease test; conditional probability shows why a positive result isn't the whole story.

title: Imaginary Island
subject: math
concept: Explore the complex plane as an island map; multiplication by i rotates you a quarter turn.

title: Rollercoaster Polynomials
subject: math
concept: Design a coaster track by choosing zeros and degree; the ride has to start and end at ground level.

title: Work Rate Crew
subject: math
concept: Schedule painting crews working at different rates; rational equations decide how long jobs take together.

title: Outbreak Model
subject: math
concept: Model a spreading rumor or virus; logarithms answer "when will it reach 1 million?"

title: Ferris Wheel
subject: math
concept: Ride a Ferris wheel and watch height trace a sine wave; change radius and speed to change the graph.

title: Undo Machine
subject: math
concept: Chain function machines, then build the machine that undoes them. Some machines can't be undone.

title: Savings Plan
subject: math
concept: Compare saving plans (add $10 a week vs double a penny a day); sequences and series show who wins and when.

title: Poll Workshop
subject: math
concept: Design a poll, pick a sample method, and see how bias and margin of error change the headline.

title: Function Family Reunion
subject: math
concept: Meet the parent functions and their transformed relatives; sliders show what each parameter does.

title: Identity Proof Race
subject: math
concept: Race to prove identities with drag-and-drop algebra steps; multiple routes to the same proof are celebrated.

title: Flight Planner
subject: math
concept: Fly a plane through crosswinds; add velocity vectors to land on the runway.

title: Image Transformer
subject: math
concept: Apply matrices to a photo to rotate, shear and stretch it; see why the order of multiplication matters.

title: Polar Rose Studio
subject: math
concept: Draw roses, spirals and cardioids with polar equations; export your art.

title: Conic Focus Finder
subject: math
concept: Slice a double cone at different angles to get circles, ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas; see real-world uses.

title: Zoom to the Limit
subject: math
concept: Zoom into a curve until it looks straight; secant lines slide into a tangent.

title: Data Desk: Distributions
subject: math
concept: Real public data sets; describe shape, center, spread and unusual features with guided prompts.

title: Design the Study
subject: math
concept: Test whether energy drinks really speed up reaction times: choose random assignment, a control group, blinding and a placebo, and a skeptical journal editor shows how each missing piece lets a hidden variable fake the result. Surveys and sampling stay with poll-workshop.

title: Game Show Strategist

title: Storm Helpers
subject: social-studies
concept: After a big storm the class walks a street to see who is affected and how (no power, a flooded road, a closed school), meets the people already helping, then picks a way kids can help and makes a poster about it.

title: Pen Pal Parcels
subject: social-studies
concept: Parcels arrive from pen pals in Ghana, Chile and Japan, each with something made there that we buy and a note on how their place changed this year; the class sends back something made here and pins each parcel on the globe.

title: Capsule From 1965
subject: social-studies
concept: Open the time capsule a class buried under the school in 1965 and pull out a photo, a letter, a lunch ticket and a toy catalog page; the class finds who made each, when and where, asks its own questions, and compares what kids liked then with now.

title: The Last Carousel Ride
subject: social-studies
concept: The town carousel stopped running in 1975; a rider and the owner's grandson remember why in different ways, and an old newspaper adds a clue. The class compares the tellings, lists possible reasons and picks the most likely.

title: Inquiry Ladder
subject: social-studies
concept: A big question about the past (Was the railroad good for our town?) sits at the top; students climb by adding supporting questions drawn from old photos, timetables and letters, mark words people disagree about, and see each rung help.

title: Source Scout
subject: social-studies
concept: For the question Should recess be longer?, scouts choose which sources to gather (a doctor's article, a survey, a toy ad, the principal's letter), weigh who might disagree, then sort each source's lines into fact and opinion to rate its trust.

title: Made for Whom?
subject: social-studies
concept: Three sources from the state's past open one at a time (a settler's diary, a railroad poster selling land, a newspaper editorial); students infer each one's audience and purpose, spot how the maker's view shaped it, and rank which helps most.

title: Why the Pony Express Ended
subject: social-studies
concept: Evidence cards from a rider's letter, a telegraph company notice, a cost ledger and a newspaper ask why the Pony Express closed after only 18 months; students build a claim, back it with evidence from two or more sources, and defend it.

title: History Article Review
subject: social-studies
concept: Students read short kid-magazine articles about the Revolution, write each one's main claim in a sentence, then check its argument and explanation (enough evidence? steps in order? voices missing?) and give a reviewer's rating with reasons.

title: School Fix-It Meeting
subject: social-studies
concept: The class picks a school problem (a long lunch line, a crowded hallway), surveys classmates and adults on why it matters to them, talks proposals through with turn-taking rules, and votes on a plan to bring to the principal.

title: Tools for Change
subject: social-studies
concept: Cards show ways people have changed things, from petitions and boycotts to letters and voting, each with a real past and present example; students pick strategies for a local problem, predict results, and turn the plan into a letter or poster.

title: Pool Repair Vote
subject: social-studies
concept: The town pool needs repairs; students hear a grandparent, a swim team parent, a shop owner and a teen lifeguard, follow the plan from problem to hearing to vote, and choose how to pay for it: taxes, entry fees or both.

title: Ripple Street
subject: social-studies
concept: Make one kid's Saturday choices on Ripple Street (rake leaves for pay or go to the park, plant flowers, play loud music) and see the costs and benefits to the kid, the rewards and fines that nudge each choice, and the ripples on neighbors.

title: Barter Bay
subject: social-studies
concept: Fishers, bakers and potters on Barter Bay trade by swapping until shells become money and trading speeds up; then the class adds too many shells, too few, or closes the cannery to see inflation, deflation and unemployment.

title: Learn and Earn
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a kid's bike repair business for a year: spend weeks learning new skills or buying better tools, and watch how many bikes you fix and what you earn compared with a friend who never trains.

title: Interest Seesaw
subject: social-studies
concept: Put birthday money in a bank, a credit union or a savings bond and watch interest add up, then borrow for a bike and watch interest add on; a seesaw shows when interest works for you and when it works against you.

title: Skateboard Fund Chances
subject: social-studies
concept: Save toward a skateboard with chance cards each month: keep money in a jar or buy shares in the class juice company that may grow or shrink; then lock, insure or risk the skateboard as rain, a cracked wheel and a theft come up.

title: Cocoa Chain
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow cocoa from a farm in Ghana through a port and a factory to a chocolate bar here; when drought hits the farms, students explain step by step, with prices and numbers, who is affected in each country and why.

title: Panel of Experts
subject: social-studies
concept: One big question (Was the Black Death a turning point?) goes to a radio panel: a historian, an economist, a geographer and a political scientist. Students mark where the experts agree, each field's key ideas, and the smaller questions each would ask.

title: Historians Disagree
subject: social-studies
concept: Two short secondary accounts explain why the Mongol Empire grew so fast; students name each central argument, sort the kinds of sources each relied on (chronicles, letters, archaeology), and judge which argument holds up better.

title: Evidence Corkboard
subject: social-studies
concept: Pin evidence from letters, maps and toll records to answer why the Erie Canal changed New York; students string each pin to the claim, tag what each piece cannot show, and list the sources they would look for next.

title: Unlabeled Archive
subject: social-studies
concept: An archive box holds a map fragment, a letter, a coin and a woodcut with no labels; students use dated reference sources to work out who made each, when, where and for whom, then decide which help answer the archivist's question.

title: Voices on the Vote
subject: social-studies
concept: Dated voices from 1789 to 1870 argue about who should vote: property owners, all white men, women, free Black men. Students place each on a timeline, trace how and why views shifted, and notice whose voices were left out.

title: Museum Label Writer
subject: social-studies
concept: Write the label for a Mesopotamian clay tablet that explains how writing began, in order and with details; fix sample labels that jump around, then rewrite yours for a kids' trail card, an audio guide and the museum website.

title: Levers of Power
subject: social-studies
concept: A dangerous crossing near school is also a state road problem and a worldwide traffic safety issue; students try levers (petition, testify, vote, write the paper, organize) through the roles citizens play and judge what each can change.

title: Motion on the Floor
subject: social-studies
concept: Run a student club meeting with an agenda, motions, amendments and a vote while respecting the minority, then compare how the same choice would be made by a city council, a jury and a family.

title: Shaping Our Week
subject: social-studies
concept: Follow a family through one week and tap each group that shapes it: the city council's bus routes, the company where a parent works, that parent's union, the food bank, the youth soccer league; remove one and see what changes.

title: Smoke and Honey
subject: social-studies
concept: A paper mill sells cheap paper while its smoke sends neighbors to the clinic, and a beekeeper's hives help nearby orchards for free; students try a tax, a filter rule or a subsidy and watch families, the business and the town.

title: Border Trade Post
subject: social-studies
concept: Two neighboring countries swap goods at a border post: first by barter, then with money, then under a tariff on imported bikes; students tally time lost, trades made and who gains or pays: shoppers, bike makers, workers and the other country.

title: The Shrinking Lake
subject: social-studies
concept: Slide through sixty years of Lake Chad as it shrinks with drought and irrigation and the population around it grows: herders, farmers and fishers move, land use changes, and four countries choose whether to fight over it or share it.

title: Missing Voices Archive
subject: social-studies
concept: A town archive on the 1918 flu holds the mayor's notices and the newspaper but few words from nurses, immigrant families or Black neighborhoods; students map whose voices are missing, how that limits the story, and which sources could fill gaps.

title: Behind the Podcast
subject: social-studies
concept: A short history podcast episode on the Great Depression comes with its show notes and source list; students trace each claim to its sources, flag sources that don't fit the claim, then compare the film's central argument with a historian's article for accuracy.

title: Claim Repair Shop
subject: social-studies
concept: Sample arguments and explanations about why World War I began arrive broken: evidence that contradicts itself, steps out of order, claims too vague; students critique each for credibility and reasoning, then repair the claim with stronger evidence.

title: Causes Web
subject: social-studies
concept: Pick a problem that is local and global at once (high rents, plastic waste) and build a web of causes from economics, geography, civics and history cards, then test whether the explanation holds up as a timeline, a chain or a loop.

title: Jury Room
subject: social-studies
concept: Twelve jurors decide a civil case about a damaged delivery; students take seats, follow deliberation rules (listen, cite evidence, check bias), reach a verdict, then compare jury deliberation with a town hall and a consensus circle.

title: Layers and Scales
subject: social-studies
concept: Make thematic maps from real data (languages, rainfall, income) at world, country and county scale, change the class breaks and watch patterns appear or vanish, then pair the map with satellite images and photos to explain a place's politics and economy.

title: Suburb Boom
subject: social-studies
concept: Watch a metro area grow from 1945 to today on aerial images as highways, home loans and zoning rules arrive and decide who can buy where; farms become subdivisions, wetlands are paved and later flood, and students change one decision to see the pattern shift.

title: Climate on the Move
subject: social-studies
concept: Four cases on a timeline (the Little Ice Age, the Dust Bowl, Sahel droughts and a recent hurricane) show how long-term climate change and sudden disasters move people, shift farming and trade, and reshape politics far away.
